To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

FALVAC1, a multiepitopie, multivalent, and multistage Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) vaccine was developed by joining epitopes from Pf vaccine antigens and a universal T helper epitote from tetanus toxiod.

the multiepitope vaccine FALVAC1, which includes epitopes from different P. falciparium vaccine candidate antigens, can induce antibodies that recognize sporozoites and blood-stage parasites and induce lymphoproliferation and IFN-g production in mice when adjuvanted with QS-21.
QS-21 and P1005 are the best adjuvants to induce immune responses to a multiepitopes multivalent vaccine against P. falciparium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective malaria vaccine that is safe and inexpensive.
the development of a vaccine against P. falciparium.
the development of a multistage, multivalent, and multiepitope vaccine candidate against Plasmodia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QS-21 is the best adjuvant in terms of eliciting immune responses to the FALVACT-1 multivalent, multiepitope multistage malaria candidate vaccine.

the use of adjuvant QS-21 in FALVAC1 formulation was able to elicit immune response to all 21 epitopes in the multiepitope vaccine construct, which is the first step towards the evaluation of the protective efficacy of this vaccine in animal models.
the adjuvant used is a very important factor in eliciting immune response to the whole FALVAC1 vaccine and to most of the individual epitopes included in it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

QS-21 is the best adjuvant in inducing high and long lasting antibody response to all the epitopes included and that the vaccine is immunogenic in outbred mice and induces antibodies that recognize the parasite.
FALVAC1 is a good candidate vaccine for further preclinical and clinical evaluation.

the vaccine FALVAC is a promising candidate vaccine that is able to elicit antibodies against all the different stages of the Plasmodium parasite and that can be improved by adding the adjuvant QS-21 to the formulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the type of epitopes included in multiepitope vaccines when selecting the most appropriate adjuvant.
the use of QS-21 as adjuvant is able to induce immune response to most epitopes in FALVAC vaccine and that this response is long-lasting.
it is possible to induce long-lasting antibody responses with a vaccine that contains multiple epitopes from several vaccine candidates and that these responses can be enhanced with adjuvants.
